strings.d1.s0.name: Rijksmuseum
strings.d1.s0.tips: Rembrandt's Night Watch and Vermeer; book a timed ticket online, opens 09:00, don't miss the library.
strings.d1.s1.name: Van Gogh Museum
strings.d1.s1.tips: Sunflowers and Almond Blossom; online tickets only, they sell out 3-7 days ahead.
strings.d1.s2.name: Museumplein Picnic
strings.d1.s2.tips: Grab sandwiches from Albert Heijn and eat on the grass; a paddling pool in summer, an ice rink in winter.
strings.d1.s3.name: Vondelpark
strings.d1.s3.tips: The city park: rent a bike, and catch the open-air theatre in summer.
strings.d1.s4.name: De Pijp & Albert Cuyp Markt
strings.d1.s4.tips: Amsterdam's biggest street market; try the stroopwafel (syrup waffle) stall (Rudi's) and the cheese.
strings.d1.b0.name: Moco Museum
strings.d1.b0.tips: Banksy and modern art; a good option if you have no Van Gogh ticket.
strings.d1.b1.name: Bakers & Roasters De Pijp
strings.d2.s0.name: Anne Frank House
strings.d2.s0.tips: Online only; tickets are released six weeks ahead on Tuesdays at 10:00. If they sell out, check the daily cancellation time.
strings.d2.s1.name: Westerkerk
strings.d2.s1.tips: The church where Rembrandt is buried; tower tours in summer.
strings.d2.s2.name: Jordaan Streets
strings.d2.s2.tips: Hofje courtyards (Karthuizerhof), Prinsengracht canals, and the Noordermarkt on Saturdays.
strings.d2.s3.name: Winkel 43
strings.d2.s3.tips: Amsterdam's most famous apple pie; on the corner of Noordermarkt.
strings.d2.s4.name: Café 't Smalle
strings.d2.s4.tips: A canalside brown café (traditional pub) open since 1786; drink a beer on the jetty.
strings.d2.b0.name: Café de Prins
strings.d2.b0.tips: A brown café opposite the Anne Frank House for lunch.
strings.d2.b1.name: Houseboat Museum
strings.d2.b1.tips: See life aboard a canal boat in the Jordaan.
strings.d3.s0.name: Dam Square & Royal Palace
strings.d3.s0.tips: Tour the Royal Palace interior; the square is calm in the morning.
strings.d3.s1.name: Begijnhof
strings.d3.s1.tips: A hidden courtyard with a wooden house; peaceful.
strings.d3.s2.name: Bloemenmarkt
strings.d3.s2.tips: The floating flower market; tulip bulbs make good souvenirs.
strings.d3.s3.name: Foodhallen
strings.d3.s3.tips: A food market in a former tram depot; try bitterballen (deep-fried meat croquettes) and Vietnamese food.
strings.d3.s4.name: Canal Cruise
strings.d3.s4.tips: A one-hour open boat trip (Those Dam Boat Guys / Flagship); the UNESCO canal ring in sunset light.
strings.d3.b0.name: Bar Brouw Ten Katestraat
strings.d3.b1.name: Amsterdam Museum
strings.d3.b1.tips: The city's history, next to the Begijnhof.
strings.d4.s0.name: Hortus Botanicus
strings.d4.s0.tips: A botanical garden from 1638, with a butterfly greenhouse.
strings.d4.s1.name: Artis Zoo
strings.d4.s1.tips: An inner-city zoo with a planetarium.
strings.d4.s2.name: Brouwerij 't IJ
strings.d4.s2.tips: A brewery beneath a windmill; order a cheese platter and the IJwit.
strings.d4.s3.name: Oosterpark
strings.d4.s3.tips: The park in the east, next to the Tropenmuseum.
strings.d4.s4.name: De Hallen Kino
strings.d4.s4.tips: A cinema and boutiques in a former tram depot; a good rainy-day option.
strings.d4.b0.name: Tropenmuseum Cafe
strings.d4.b0.tips: The cafe of the world cultures museum.
strings.d4.b1.name: NEMO Science Museum Roof
strings.d4.b1.tips: A free rooftop terrace on the ship-shaped museum, with views of the harbour.
strings.d5.s0.name: Centraal Ferry Buiksloterweg
strings.d5.s0.tips: A free ferry from behind the station; 3 minutes.
strings.d5.s1.name: A'DAM Lookout
strings.d5.s1.tips: An observation deck on the north shore with the Over the Edge swing.
strings.d5.s2.name: EYE Filmmuseum
strings.d5.s2.tips: The white bird-shaped building; exhibitions and a cafe, with views over the water.
strings.d5.s3.name: NDSM Werf
strings.d5.s3.tips: Street art and container cafes in a former shipyard; take ferry 906.
strings.d5.s4.name: Pllek NDSM
strings.d5.s4.tips: A restaurant in a shipping container; beach chairs and views over the IJ.
strings.d5.b0.name: Café de Ceuvel
strings.d5.b0.tips: A sustainable canalside cafe in Noord.
strings.d5.b1.name: Noorderpark
strings.d5.b1.tips: The northern park, instead of NDSM.
strings.d6.s0.name: Zaanse Schans Windmills
strings.d6.s0.tips: 20 minutes by train (Zaandijk); working windmills (entry 5-6 EUR) and green wooden houses. Go before the morning tour buses arrive.
strings.d6.s1.name: Catharina Hoeve Cheese Farm
strings.d6.s2.name: Zaanse Schans Clog Workshop
strings.d6.s2.tips: A demonstration of wooden shoe making.
strings.d6.s3.name: De Hoop op d'Swarte Walvis
strings.d6.s3.tips: A historic restaurant in Zaanse; fish and Dutch cuisine.
strings.d6.s4.name: Haarlem Grote Markt
strings.d6.s4.tips: Stop in Haarlem on the way back; the cathedral square and the Jopen beer church.
strings.d6.b0.name: Haarlem Jopenkerk
strings.d6.b1.name: Volendam & Marken
strings.d6.b1.tips: A fishing town and an island, instead of Haarlem.
strings.d7.s0.name: De 9 Straatjes
strings.d7.s0.tips: The Nine Streets: vintage shops, design and canal corners.
strings.d7.s1.name: Stubbe's Haring
strings.d7.s1.tips: A herring stand on a canal corner; eat it with onion and pickles, a Dutch ritual.
strings.d7.s2.name: Van Stapele Koekmakerij
strings.d7.s2.tips: One kind of cookie only (with white chocolate); expect a 20-minute queue.
strings.d7.s3.name: Amsterdam Centraal
strings.d7.s3.tips: 15 minutes by train to Schiphol; time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Café Luxembourg
strings.d7.b1.name: Spui Book Market
strings.d7.b1.tips: The Friday book market, instead of the streets.
strings.note0: Get around by bike or on foot; the GVB day pass is 9 EUR, and the train to Schiphol takes 15 minutes. Don't walk in the bike lane (cyclists will ring their bells).
strings.note1: Rijks, Van Gogh, Anne Frank: timed tickets online only; Anne Frank tickets are released six weeks ahead on Tuesdays at 10:00.
strings.note2: Summer is 20-24°C with changeable weather, so bring a raincoat. Vondelpark, canal jetties and open boats; the Grachtenfestival takes place in August.
strings.note3: Eat stroopwafel hot at the market, herring from the stand, and bitterballen in a brown café; coffee is 3.5 EUR, beer 5 EUR.
strings.note4: A coffeeshop is not a cafe; photography is forbidden in the Red Light District. Round up the bill to tip.
strings.note5: Take the Sprinter from Centraal to Zaanse Schans (20 minutes); go before 10:00.
